title: Exponential lower bounds for unrestricted perfect secret sharing
formal: Do constants c>0 and n₀ exist such that, for every n≥n₀, some monotone access structure Γ on [n] requires max_i log₂|S_i|/log₂|S|≥2^(cn) in every perfect secret-sharing scheme for a uniform secret in an arbitrary finite alphabet S with |S|≥2?
definitions: Γ⊆2^[n] is upward closed, excludes ∅ and includes [n]. A scheme is a joint distribution of a uniformly distributed secret over a finite alphabet S and shares X_i in finite alphabets S_i. For every A∈Γ a deterministic function of (X_i)_{i∈A} equals S with probability one. For every A∉Γ the share vector (X_i)_{i∈A} is statistically independent of S. There is no linearity, efficiency or restriction on reconstruction functions. Share size counts the logarithm of its alphabet size, not its entropy or the total size of all shares. The structure may depend on n and need not be explicitly constructed.

context_blocks.text: Perfect secret sharing implements an arbitrary policy specifying which coalitions may recover a secret. General constructions use exponentially long shares, while unconditional lower bounds for unrestricted schemes are much smaller.

The cited work proves an exponential alternative involving share length or the description of reconstruction. That does not prove an exponential share lower bound when reconstruction is unrestricted. The existing upper-bound card asks whether every access structure has smaller shares; this conjecture asks for genuinely difficult structures with a different quantitative target.

why: Determine whether exponential information overhead is unavoidable for some access policies, without assumptions on linearity or computation.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
